text:
maya: FYI bringing up Hyacinth-8.3b (community) — seeing weird token drift when we run q4_0 quant on runtime v2.6. Suspect KV cache eviction / RoPE interaction. Can someone pick this up? :eyes:

ash: I can take an initial pass. Quick question — is this observed only on long-context tests or small prompts too?

maya: Small prompts are OK. Fails start showing up reliably past ~1024 tokens (truncation/regression in continuation). Repro steps in a sec.

dmitri: is Hyacinth using rotary or ALiBi? Could matter for how we handle cached positions.

maya: It's a hybrid: RoPE variant with position scaling (not standard rotary). Model metadata: attention_type=scaled_rope, kv_layout=separate, chunked_kv=true.

ash: nice. please paste minimal repro and the runtime flags you used.

maya: repro (local runtime v2.6, q4_0):
```
# start server
./run_runtime --model hyacinth-8.3b --quant q4_0 --engine v2.6 --kv-cache true --max-seq 2048
# client prompt (repeat token to reach >1024)
PROMPT = "Nonsense " * 1200
# generate with streaming off, temp 0.0
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt": "'"$PROMPT"'", "max_tokens": 50}'
```
Observed: at token ~1026, generation repeats a substring and drops into loop. Not deterministic on exact token but >= 1024 boundary.

lee: any differences if you disable chunked_kv?

maya: disabling chunked_kv on the same binary -> behavior disappears. So chunked_kv + q4_0 + scaled_rope seems like the combo.

dmitri: hypothesis: quant kernel uses packed buffers sized to chunk boundary and we have an off-by-one when rotating cached keys vs newly computed positions. Could be buffer aliasing in q4_0 path.

ash: agrees. Plan: (1) reproduce with runtime debug logs (kv indices, position ids) (2) add a unit test that stresses >1024 boundary with small tokens (3) try q8_0 and q4_1 to see if kernels differ.

maya: I ran q8_0 quickly — no regression on same prompt. q4_1 untested.

triage-bot: Assigned #eng-ml to @ash for initial debug and @dmitri for kernel review. ETA 48h.

ash: starting with reproducer + log patch. Pasting debug flag I used: `--kv-debug --rope-check --dump-kv=kv_dump.json`

dmitri: I'll instrument the q4_0 packing code to emit offsets where pack sizes != expected_chunk_size. Also will add a small fuzz that toggles chunk boundaries.

maya: also add eval harness: run our standard llm-evals promptset (sensitivity/regression suite) with both q4_0 and q8_0, and compare BLEU/EM-like metrics for continuations. We need an automated alert if drop >2% on any core prompt.

lee: note for production: if we can't resolve soon, fallback policy should route Hyacinth q4_0 requests to q8_0 or to unquantized fallback on Dedicated. We should add route policy: `model.hyacinth: if quant==q4_0 and context>1024 -> fallback:q8_0`

maya: good. For the ticket, let's capture: repro steps, runtime flags, relevant model metadata, quick eval number for q8_0 vs q4_0 (when available), and suggested runtime mitigation (fallback routing).

ash: I'll open a proper issue and link the kv_dump and logs. Posting a quick grep snippet for later debugging:
```
grep "kv_idx" kv_dump.json | head -n 40
# lines show repeated idx 256-263 around token 1024 boundary
```

ash: quick note — observed that when running with `--max-seq 2048 --prefill 1024` the mem offsets shift by 8 bytes in the q4_0 path vs q8_0. suspicious.

dmitri: that's the aliasing symptom I expected. Could be int32 vs int64 indexing mismatch in pack routine. I'll run a small reproducer on CPU kernel to validate.

maya: awesome. tagging @platform on infra for a reserved node if you need longer runs.

triage-bot: Next actions: ash(repro+logs), dmitri(kernel instrument), maya(eval harness + fallback policy). ETA 48h.

ash: starting now, will post first results in this thread. :thumbsup:
